set_aside.subject: R0-36 replay protection after ordinary record changes
set_aside.text: This holds while the record the first create made keeps its values
set_aside.question: Which changes make a created record no longer 'keep its values' and therefore end replay recognition: only the erasure/anonymisation named next, changes to create-input fields, or any later state change such as correction, archive, restriction or ending a relationship?
options: Only customer erasure and project anonymisation end replay recognition
A correction of a create-input value also ends replay recognition
Any change to the record ends replay recognition
set_aside.default_guess: Only customer erasure, whole project deletion and project anonymisation end replay recognition; ordinary corrections and state changes retain it.

witness.initial: A customer was recorded successfully, but the response was lost.
events: The owner corrects that customer's e-mail before the original record-customer request is retried.
The caller retries the original create request with the same request identity.
outcomes: Registry recognises the retry and returns the existing, now-corrected Customer without creating another.
Because the record no longer keeps all its original values, Registry treats the retry as a new create and makes a second Customer.
witness.observer: The owner sees either one or two Customers.

set_aside.subject: R0-36 replay after anonymisation with a caller-supplied project id
set_aside.text: a create repeated after that is a new create, and its answer shows the new record it made
set_aside.question: When the original project create supplied an id and the anonymised project still keeps that id, must the retry create a project under a different id, reuse the occupied id, or be refused for the id conflict?
options: Mint a different id and return the new project
Reuse the supplied id despite the anonymised record retaining it
Refuse because the supplied id is still occupied
The new-create exception does not apply to creates with caller-supplied ids
set_aside.default_guess: Refuse the retry because the anonymised project still owns the supplied id.

witness.initial: In an instance where caller-supplied project ids are allowed, project P was created with id X, later archived and anonymised; the anonymised record still retains id X.
events: The caller repeats the lost-answer create request, again supplying id X.
outcomes: The new R0-36 passage treats it as a new create and returns a newly made record.
R0-62 and R0-87 keep the anonymised record under X, while R0-07 refuses a create whose supplied id conflicts, so no new record is made.
witness.observer: The caller sees either a successful new project or a refusal.

set_aside.subject: R0-36 replay after whole project deletion
set_aside.text: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat
set_aside.question: What happens to replay recognition when the owner chooses the other project-erasure mode and deletes the archived project whole?
options: Whole deletion also removes replay recognition, so the retry is a new create
A replay tombstone survives whole deletion and prevents a second project
The retry is refused because the former id or request identity remains reserved
set_aside.default_guess: Whole deletion also removes replay recognition, and a later retry is a new create.

witness.initial: A project create succeeded without a caller-supplied id, but its response was lost; the project was later archived and deleted whole.
events: The caller repeats the original create request with the same request identity.
outcomes: Registry retained replay evidence outside the deleted project and returns or refuses based on the former create without making another project.
Registry deleted the replay evidence with the project and creates a new project.
witness.observer: The owner and caller see whether a new project appears.

set_aside.subject: R0-36 scope of the erasure exception across create actions
set_aside.text: a create repeated after that is a new create
set_aside.question: Does this exception apply only to recreating the erased Customer or anonymised Project, or also to creates of records removed with them, especially a room removed when its project is anonymised?
options: Only record-customer and create-project retries receive the new-create treatment
Every create whose replay evidence was removed receives the new-create treatment
Nested creates remain subject to their current parent-state failures
set_aside.default_guess: The exception applies only to creation of the erased Customer or anonymised Project; a room retry remains refused because its project is archived and anonymised.

witness.initial: A room was added to a project and its response was lost; the project was later archived and anonymised, removing its rooms.
events: Cabinet Kernel retries the original add-room request with the same request identity.
outcomes: Because anonymisation removed everything identifying the retry, R0-36 treats it as a new room create.
The add-room contract refuses it because the project is archived, and an anonymised project has no rooms to which one can be added.
witness.observer: Cabinet Kernel sees either a newly created room or a refusal.
